concepts.name: Project versus ongoing operations
concepts.summary: Explain that a project is temporary, has a unique outcome and a defined end, unlike repeating day-to-day operations.

concepts.name: Triple constraint
concepts.summary: Describe how scope, time and cost are linked so that changing one usually affects the others and quality.

concepts.name: Project roles
concepts.summary: Identify what the sponsor, project manager, team members and other stakeholders do on a project.

concepts.name: Tasks, deliverables and milestones
concepts.summary: Distinguish work activities from the tangible outputs they produce and from zero-duration checkpoints.

concepts.name: Project life cycle phases
concepts.summary: Recall the phases of a waterfall-style project: initiating, planning, executing, monitoring and controlling, and closing.

concepts.name: Project charter purpose
concepts.summary: Explain that a charter formally authorises the project and records its purpose, objectives, sponsor and the manager's authority.

concepts.name: Stakeholders
concepts.summary: Define stakeholders as people or groups affected by or able to influence the project, and name typical examples.

misconceptions.text: A project is any work the team does repeatedly, such as monthly reporting.
A project manager personally does most of the project's technical work.
Stakeholders are only the people who work on the project team.

concepts.name: Writing a scope statement
concepts.summary: Write a scope statement listing deliverables, boundaries, exclusions, assumptions and acceptance criteria for a small project.

concepts.name: Building a work breakdown structure
concepts.summary: Decompose project deliverables into hierarchical work packages that cover all the scope and nothing more.

concepts.name: Estimating task durations
concepts.summary: Produce duration estimates for work packages using expert judgement, analogous comparison and simple three-point estimates.

concepts.name: Task dependencies
concepts.summary: Sequence activities using finish-to-start, start-to-start, finish-to-finish and start-to-finish links, with lead and lag.

concepts.name: Reading and drawing Gantt charts
concepts.summary: Build and interpret a Gantt chart showing task bars, dependencies, milestones and progress against a timeline.

concepts.name: Basic cost estimation
concepts.summary: Estimate costs for labour, materials and other items from the WBS and total them into a simple budget.

concepts.name: Simple risk identification
concepts.summary: Identify uncertain events that could help or harm objectives and distinguish them from issues already occurring.

misconceptions.text: A WBS is a list of tasks in time order, like a schedule.
If a task is not mentioned in the scope statement, the team should do it anyway to please the client.
A risk is the same thing as a problem that is already happening.

concepts.name: Critical path analysis
concepts.summary: Compute forward and backward passes to find the longest path and determine the minimum project duration.

concepts.name: Float and slack
concepts.summary: Calculate total and free float and analyse which tasks can slip without delaying the finish date.

concepts.name: Resource allocation and levelling
concepts.summary: Analyse resource loads across the schedule, resolve overallocation and understand the effect on the end date.

concepts.name: Risk register and scoring
concepts.summary: Maintain a register that scores risks by probability and impact, assigns owners and records responses.

concepts.name: Risk response strategies
concepts.summary: Select and justify avoid, transfer, mitigate or accept responses for individual risks.

concepts.name: Budget baseline and contingency
concepts.summary: Build a time-phased budget with contingency from the cost estimates and schedule.

concepts.name: Stakeholder analysis and communication plan
concepts.summary: Analyse stakeholders' influence and interest and design who receives which information, how and how often.

concepts.name: Status tracking and reporting
concepts.summary: Track percent complete and actual versus planned dates and cost and report variances clearly.

misconceptions.text: The critical path is the path with the most important or most expensive tasks.
Tasks with float can be delayed indefinitely without consequence.
Adding more people to a late task always shortens it proportionally.

concepts.name: Earned value analysis
concepts.summary: Use planned value, earned value and actual cost to compute schedule and cost variances and performance indices.

concepts.name: Forecasting completion
concepts.summary: Evaluate which estimate-at-completion formula fits the situation and judge whether the budget and deadline are achievable.

concepts.name: Schedule compression
concepts.summary: Evaluate crashing and fast-tracking options for recovering schedule against their cost and risk impact.

concepts.name: Quantitative schedule risk
concepts.summary: Evaluate schedule confidence using PERT estimates and simulation rather than single-point durations.

concepts.name: Scope creep control
concepts.summary: Analyse how uncontrolled additions arise and apply baselines and acceptance criteria to contain them.

concepts.name: Integrated change control
concepts.summary: Run changes through a formal process that assesses impact on scope, schedule, cost and risk before approval and updates the baselines.

concepts.name: Managing stakeholder expectations
concepts.summary: Judge engagement approaches for resistant or conflicting stakeholders and negotiate trade-offs among priorities.

concepts.name: Issue and escalation management
concepts.summary: Analyse issues, assign owners and decide when and how to escalate beyond the project manager's authority.

misconceptions.text: A positive cost variance alone means the project is healthy.
Crashing and fast-tracking are the same and both only cost money.
Small change requests can be accepted informally if the sponsor asks.

concepts.name: Tailoring the planning approach
concepts.summary: Judge when a plan-driven approach, a hybrid or an adaptive one suits a project's uncertainty, constraints and governance.

concepts.name: Critical chain and buffer management
concepts.summary: Evaluate critical chain scheduling, with resource constraints and shared buffers, against traditional critical path control.

concepts.name: Designing project controls
concepts.summary: Design governance, stage gates, thresholds and reporting that fit the project's size, risk and organisational context.

concepts.name: Portfolio-level trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate competing projects' priorities and shared resources to make defensible trade-offs and recommendations.

concepts.name: Recovering a failing project
concepts.summary: Diagnose root causes of failure and create a recovery plan, including re-baselining, descoping or termination.

concepts.name: Contract and procurement risk
aliases: fixed price vs time and materials
concepts.summary: Evaluate contract types and vendor arrangements for how they allocate cost and schedule risk.

concepts.name: Benefits realisation and lessons learned
concepts.summary: Create closure practices that confirm acceptance, transfer handover, measure benefits and feed lessons into future planning.

misconceptions.text: A project delivered on time and on budget is automatically a success.
Adding more reporting and controls always improves project performance.
Re-baselining a late project resolves the underlying problems.
